utterances.text: Thank you, General. And hopefully that will address the points raised in Mr. Fila's cross and the concerns of the Trial Chamber in that regard. I apologise for the confusion caused, General. Now, I'd like to talk about another factor, going back to now my originally planned cross. During the course of your direct examination the other day, you indicated that on the ground there were many -- I believe -- I don't have the transcript in front of me, but you said rumours and misinformation circulating during the chaotic wartime circumstances. For that reason, I would like to start by having you clarify for us things that we heard other people talk about. Specifically, what we had witnesses from military security, or the VB, talk about from their sources outside Kosovo and Metohija, and I want to find out what, if anything, about this information was available to you at the command of the Pristina Corps in 1999 in the middle of the war. And specifically, I want to ask you whether you had any credible or verified information about the existence of a so-called para-police formation named the Vukovi sa Drine, the Wolves of the Drina, led by Nedeljko Legenda, or Legend, Karisik or anyone else for that matter operating under the auspices of the Serbian MUP based in Kosovo Polje. Did you have any such information of a credible or verifiable nature at the Pristina Corps command?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any information, let alone verifiable, reliable. No information whatsoever. I didn't even have any initial information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to focus for the first part of my cross-examination relating to the time period of 1998 to try and understand how the various terminology in various military documents applies to the situation in the field. Now, first of all, I would like to look at Exhibit 4D129. And once that gets up on the screen, we will proceed with that. In order to try and speed things up a bit, I will try and -- I will not have you read the entire document into the record, but I will highlight what portions of it are necessary. This appears to be a regular combat report of the 3rd Army command dated the 20th of June, 1998. It bears in the upper left strictly confidential number 3988-58, and it appears to be sent to the General Staff. And we will see later when we get to the last page that indeed it has -- it was issued by General Dusan Samardzic. I would like to first focus on page 2 of the B/C/S, which is also page 2 of the English. Specifically the section number 5, or paragraph 5, that starts with "I have decided." And the part -- the part that starts, 5.1, "Proposal of decision." Wherein General Samardzic says, as you can see on the screen there, that -- where it says: "I propose the following decision: Engage part of the army forces in cooperation with forces of the MUP, Ministry of the Interior, of the Republic of Serbia to ensure the flee flow of traffic on the Pristina-Stimlje-Suva Reka-Prizren road." And further: "Ensure the free flow of traffic along the road by taking and holding passes and road junctions, controlling the approaches leading to the road, and patrolling the road itself." Now, would you agree with me that this proposal by General Samardzic includes a proposal for engagement of both VJ and Serbian MUP forces for this coordinated action?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to provide a full answer, I will require the next page as well, but I'm going to try to answer this part of the question now. In paragraph 5, the commander of the 3rd Army decided to use the units subordinated to him to be engaged in the border belt. Full stop. Then he proposes to the chief of General Staff on the basis of some order that he invokes here that, had been issued by General Perisic, how to use MUP forces in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija from the point of view of carrying out the task of controlling the territory. And if I remember this document correctly, at the end he is going to propose to General Perisic that at the level of the General Staff and the ministry up there in Belgrade, this subject matter be defined. However, I am saying this on the basis of memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That, I think, is generally speaking the -- the document we're talking about. If we could move to the next page in the B/C/S and English, I think we'll see, General, there where the forces that are to be engaged are identified based upon forces of the 3rd Army and forces of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. Does this, in fact, bear out the point we are trying to make on the last page that General Samardzic proposes forces from both structures to be utilised for this coordinated joint action in 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is borne out by that. The protection of the main roads. With your permission, the last sentence here reads as follows: "Please coordinate the use of MUP forces at the level of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia and the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia." Because he cannot decide on that. So coordination at top state level, military and police, that has to be regulated in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether we had page 2 up on the screen. I'd asked for page 2, but it looks like we're on page 3. But in any event, page 2 as the document speaks for itself identifies the specific units from both structures that are to be used in this action being proposed by General Samardzic. Now, if we can move on while remaining in 1998 -- well, first of all, this particular proposed action, am I correct that the initial proposal for it came from within the Pristina Corps and was communicated upwards to General Samardzic at the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the leave of the Honourable Trial Chamber, I have to say that this is not a proposal for an action. This is a proposal for a longer-term engagement, carrying out a longer-lasting task of ensuring the territory and protecting the main roads in Kosovo and Metohija. That is the core of the matter. It is not one single action. In my view -- well, I don't know where this proposal came from. It will be quite understandable if the proposal came from the command of the Pristina Corps vis-a-vis the command of the 3rd Army and that this was coordinated with the MUP staff in Pristina. However, all of that is a question of my own assessment as to what it was that was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The issue brought up was whether it was a long-term action or an action. It's my fault, due to my lack of knowing enough Serbian to be doing all of this in Serbian. The English is rather bulky in that regard. So I appreciate the correction -- or clarification of that matter. Now, if we could remain in 1998 and focus some more on the communication between the MUP and the VJ during this period. I would ask for 6D692 to be called up in e-court so that we can discuss it briefly. And once it comes up on the screen, I think you'll see that this is a preparatory order that at the top indicates that it originated from the Pristina Corps command. Strictly confidential number 880-176, dated 7 August 1998, and reflecting that it was sent to the personal attention of the commander of the -- the komandant, NS. I don't think we have an English one in the system, so I will try to highlight through you the section I would to refer to. First of all, if we look at the bottom of the document, it has underneath the signature, what in the Serbian says "dostaviti or send to. And under B, it has "sifrom" or encoded, the 125th and 549th Motorised Brigades and says Ikmprk. Is this in fact the same forward command post of the Pristina Corps in Djakovica that we have previously heard you testify about where you were in 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Just waiting for the transcript to catch up with us. And does that mean that you have personal knowledge of this document having received it in -- at around the time that it was issued?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document follows the previous map, entitled "Ratis." It's the same time, the same action, the same event, around Radonjic Gorezero, Lake Radonjic. This is just a preparatory document for using the army units and the MUP in carrying out this task, as the heading says.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, just waiting for the transcript to catch up with us in the English. I appreciate that. I'm just trying to use the documents to establish what the manner of creation of these documents was in 1998 so we can better understand the interrelation between the various entities. Now, the -- you say this is a preparatory document for using army and MUP to carry out tasks in this engagement. Am I correct that in this document your superior, General Pavkovic, is tasking you with immediately beginning preparations for carrying out the action to support MUP units in the area of Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you are suggesting and asking about cannot be seen from this document. The only thing that is being done here is ordering officers to gather at the forward command post, those whose units are being engaged. And who is going to use the units, this is not ordered by the corps commander, whether he is going to authorise me or whether he personally is going to carry out this preparation. If you wish to go into detail, in paragraph 7 he only orders me, as the Chief of Staff, to set the structure of Combat Group 52 according to this task.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... as opposed to 3rd Army. But let me -- let me ask this question: Am I correct that simultaneous with the issuing of this proposed preparatory order, that in fact the organs of the Pristina Corps prepared on Odluka, or decision map, for this action and that both were presented for approval by General Samardzic before any engagement of the VJ or MUP forces was actually effectuated, or undertaken?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is the procedure, the inviolable procedure, if I can put it that way. But let's get this clear. And I hope that the Trial Chamber will understand me if I say a sentence or two more in terms of when this was, when the MUP and army units were being engaged. The commander of the army does not make a decision on the engagement of MUP units. He makes a decision to engage army units, and within this task in which the MUP units participate as well. I would like us to be precise on this so that this would be of use to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact the Odluka, or decision map, contains, as we've seen, both the information necessary for the VJ forces or units and the information necessary for the MUP forces or units for that particular engagement or coordinated action; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the instructions for work maps of the Army of Yugoslavia, on the decision map one enters one's own forces and other forces from the defence system. The enemy forces, the capacity of the territory. So yes, that is the case that what is entered on the map are the MUP forces too, to the extent to which one has the right information available as to how and where they are being engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have personal knowledge of the fact that General Samardzic approved this action before it was undertaken?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only ten minutes ago we saw the decision map that he had approved. And I know that in combat reports of the command of the 3rd Army that the previous decision was made for Glodjane, and I know that he informed the General Staff after this action was over. May I be allowed to say that I know that the commander of the 3rd Army came personally to the area when the corpses were found and when the action was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: According to the instructions and the procedure -- and the procedure, the inviolable procedure, as you stated it, am I correct, then, that this would be the method by which all actions were planned in 1998; that is to say, that all actions had a Odluka map that was proposed by the VJ -- VJ officer preparing it and then approved by the VJ superior officer authorising it? And that's my first question. Would that be the standard operating procedure in 1998 for the actions that were undertaken -- the joint coordinated actions that were undertaken during that time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do I understand that procedure correctly that once -- once a VJ commander has signed his approval upon a Odluka, or decision map, only he can change the same; so that is to say, the VJ officer who signed and authorised and approved the decision map.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be according to regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we move on. I'd like to move ahead to 1999. And to begin with, I'd like to clarify a point that came up in your examination the other day. But first of all -- yeah. If we could look at 6D1416 very briefly. And I think you dealt with a similar document in your direct examination dealing with an action for the other part of Drenica in March of 1999. This deals with, I believe, Gornje Drenica. But if we can look at this. First of all, this is a document from the command of the Pristina Corps. Strictly confidential document number 455-43, dated the 18th of March, 1999 and directed to the commander of the 3rd Army to his personal -- or to -- to him personally. Now, if I could --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just -- I just want to say for the record that it's very difficult, as I've pointed out before, to deal with untranslated documents. There may be matters in these documents that would be appropriate for further examination by me, and there's no way I can tell. And we seem to just go from one untranslated document to another today since we've done this. And I'm -- I'm sympathetic with the position of Mr. Ivetic in regard to this, because it's not his fault that he doesn't have untranslated -- translated document, I'm sure, but it does cause a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I appreciate the difficulties. In fact, I have, I think, spoken on the difficulties of untranslated documents in the past as well. Thankfully in each of the teams we have some B/C/S speakers, so that alleviate the problem somewhat. This particular document was one that came up because of an issue that arose in court, I believe, on the 9th of November where a similar document was utilised and there was -- there actually was an English translation of that document, and then there was a lot of confusion because the translation of the document was suspect. And I'm actually -- this procedure will, I think, be useful to actually not only get information necessary for the Trial Chamber to have the full picture in front -- in front of it, but also I hope it will clear up the translation issue from the other day rather soundly, so that there will be no doubt in anyone's mind what the document from the other day actually said. So that's -- that's the -- what I plan to do with this document, and then, of course, referring back to the document that was referred to in court and introduced -- and actually commented on -- commented on by Mr. Ackerman, since I think he's the one that noted the -- the translation issue in the -- in the prior document, which is going to be 5D276, which was used, I believe, on the 9th of November in the direction of Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: May I just say, Your Honour, that raises another issue that has been rattling around in my mind for some weeks now. The translators in the booths in this courtroom do an outstanding job under very, very difficult conditions, and I don't by my remarks tend to take anything away from them at all, but their job is to do the best they can under the circumstances. CLSS, on the other hand, can take time and expend great effort at properly translating a document to try to get it as accurate as possible. And I -- I think it is -- is contrary to a rather well-oiled system for us to try to use in-court translators for precise translations of documents in lieu of CLSS translations that are more carefully thought out and -- and worked on. And I -- I notice we've been doing that, on occasion having the booth translate sentences from documents to check if CLSS has done them right. I think it maybe is backwards. And I just wanted to make that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I imagine everyone is well aware of all the efforts that have been made by everyone involved and particularly by the legal staff of this Trial Chamber to try to organise the translation of documents in a way which will facilitate the fair and expeditious conduct of this trial. With the best will in the world and recognising that we do not live in a perfect world, there will from time to time be problems. When they arise, if a facility is readily available, then it will be used. And by that I'm referring to the interpretation in court. If there's a difficulty still, then it's open to any party to re-submit the document or submit it to CLSS and make a filing that draws our attention to some inconsistency. The important thing is that every counsel has made every effort to prioritise the request for translation. Mr. Ivetic has explained that this particular document comes into play because of something that occurred fairly recently in the evidence. I hope, however, that the ones which you intend to use and knew you would be likely to use with this witness have, so far as possible, been translated as a matter of priority. It has been known for some time that General Lazarevic was likely to be a witness. So please proceed with this one as quickly as you can on the basis of the use of interpretation because of the circumstances you have explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to clarify, I do not intend the in-court interpretation to try and correct a mistranslation in the English. It's, rather, to alleviate confusion arising from a rather complicated formulation in the Serbian. And the translation in English of the document 5D297 is indeed correct, but the -- the meaning behind the same is a little bit unclear and will be clear as we go through this -- through this series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, first of all, so we can set everyone on the same page with -- with respect to what this document is, I've already, I believe, read the source of the document, the date, et cetera. If I can ask you, sir, to read for us the subject line that begins: "y komandu korpusa" And in doing so, tell us whether you recall authoring such a document and planning such an engagement in the Drenica and the Podujevo regions or the Podujevo Road regions. And I see my -- counsel is on his feet. General, could you do that for us, sir, could you read the introductory paragraph for this order or act of the command of the Pristina Corps. And that begins: "y komandu korpusa," in the command of the corps.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Within the corps command, the planning and preparation of the commands of units and forces of the MUP has been carried out for performing actions to crush Siptar terrorist forces in the area of Northern Drenica and Podujevo in keeping with your general concept and specific plans." You asked me further on whether I was aware of what document this is, and my answer is this: This document follows from a number of prior documents dated in the month of February when the army command ordered the corps command to perform general planning without indicating the dates when these actions would be carried out. And in response to the question of my Defence counsel whether I knew whether MUP planned its own -- did its own planning for these actions, I said "yes." And this is specific coordination between two structures just before the specific implementation of this task. And I would like the Trial Chamber to allow me to show that this is reflective of the general concept of how army units are used. The commander has the right and duty to propose decisions in keeping with the decision of his superior commander, and the decision is ultimately verified by his subordinate officer. This document reflects strict subordination within the units of the Pristina Corps and the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. And, again, I apologise. I heard you, but the transcript was catching up in English. So that was the reason for the pause. If we can just focus on -- briefly on section 2.1 and 2.2 for the non-B/C/S speakers in here, General, I will just paraphrase the units that are involved. And if I err in any way, I would ask that you intervene and correct me. But this document deals with the engagement of Battle Group 125-1, the 257th -- 252nd Motorised Brigade of the armoured brigade, Battle Group 15-2. And then in the section 1, "Vut Gornakin" [phoen], it says: "4 Ceta" or detachments of the PJP. In 2.2 we have Battle group 15-4, 15-1, 125-4 and then 6 Ceta or detachments of the MUP. This will become important as we turn to the next page of the document. And, General, I would focus your attention to item 6, labeled [Interpretation] "Problems and omissions in the action." [In English] And I would ask you, it seems that in planning for this engagement you noted a shortage -- or someone -- the operatives in the Pristina Corps noted a shortage of four Ceta, or detachments, of MUP PJP. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's Note: Ceta is "company," not "detachment."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is a very self-explanatory document, which indicates that the corps command knows exactly which of its forces would be engaged, but it's very complicated for me to comment on everything that you have just read. At any rate, the person from the MUP who came to effect the coordination probably did not know and didn't bring accurate information on the available forces of the MUP, did not know their names and their designation. And it was the task of the group from the corps command in charge of coordination that the MUP forces available were not sufficient to perform this assigned task in the area of Podujevo and Northern Drenica. That is why I inform the army commander that not all the problems had been resolved that needed to be resolved in order to start the coordinating planning of this action.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again, General, I apologise. We had to wait for the transcript to catch up with us. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, every time you say that, you add to the work of the interpreter. I think the witness knows very well by now what you're doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Some habits are hard to -- to drop at the drop of a hat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, General, if we can look at the last two lines of this document. It would appear that the Pristina Corps request an engagement of additional units of the MUP to make up for this shortfall, or shortage. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The principle of coordination and organisation of coordinated action is a principle of agreement of two or more parties in the performance of a specific joint task. So it must have been the general belief and assessment, although this document was signed by me and the Pristina Corps stands behind it -- it must have been the assessment that MUP forces were insufficient, a request was made for additional forces. And I would like to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to this last sentence, which is very important. In that sentence, I propose that additional coordinated action in the field be effected through reconnaissance by commanders and combat groups and parts of units of the MUP whereby the process of coordinated action would be finalised at this lowest level. I also proposed the time and the method for doing that, to organise additional reconnaissance on the 19th of March. I cannot order the MUP to do that. I can just suggest it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... You cannot actually make any -- any -- anything beyond that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to go into this area I wanted to clear up. If we look at this -- these last two line, would you therefore agree with me that the formulation in Serbian that begins [Interpretation] The request of the MUP has been submitted to engage additional forces." [In English] Now, will you agree with me that this formation is actually clumsily written, and it should be [Interpretation] A request has been submitted to -- [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... from the MUP. Do you see the confusion that I'm -- that I'm talking about now, General?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Serbian language is not perfect. I understand you. I understand what you're saying. I'm addressing my superior commander and informing him that this group for coordination evaluated that MUP forces were not sufficient and that MUP should be required to give additional forces. Not that MUP should ask for additional forces from somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... which is the document that was used the other day that had some confusion as to what it meant. And I believe from reviewing the transcript, that we -- it was concluded at that point in time that the request came from the MUP to the VJ, rather than the other way around. And if we could look at the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's the number of the document, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 5D276, Your Honour. Which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: For some reason, I've noted earlier 5D297. Is that ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I -- if I did say that, I misspoke. It should be 5D276.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman already apprised me that the transcript had that wrong number in there, and I think it's my fault. So 5D276, which is the document we used the other day. If we could just focus on the last two lines of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, do we have here in this document written, I believe, the exact same day as the document we have just looked at, do we see the same formulation here: [Interpretation] A MUP request was submitted." [In English] And having looked at this other document, 6D146 that we just looked through, would you agree with me now that in this case we cannot exclude the possibility that the request was sent to the MUP rather than coming from the MUP in this particular document for which we do have an English translation.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right. It's an error, basically a typo. Essentially we understand each other. This is a similar proposal for another action in that broader area. It's also a proposed idea how to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you saying there is a typo error in the Serb version?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. If you allow me to say, translated into Serbian it would mean "a request of the MUP has been submitted to engage their forces." Whereas, in fact it should read "a request has been submitted to the MUP." This little "A" after "MUP" should be the letter "U" in Serbian, to indicate a different name case, "to the MUP."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And so now, as you see, Your Honours, my beef is not with the translation. It's the fact that the translation incorporates the typo in it. And I hope that it was now clearer than it was the other day to everyone that the request flows from the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move on, General, with respect to -- still 1999. First of all, the other day you mentioned that sort of as a -- symbolic of the -- of the frustrations or the problems arising from the re-subordination issue that a certain army commander - I believe it was Mitrovic Dragan and some other VJ staff - were -- were casualties as a result of a lapse in a coordinated action. Do you recall, sir, that in fact those casualties occurred on the 20th of April before the issue of re-subordination was on the table by way of a re-subordination order issued by yourself?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my understanding that the esteemed Defence counsel said Dragan Mitrovic -- I believe the Trial Chamber would allow me to say this. I mean, it was probably Dragan Mikovic [phoen] of the 37th Brigade was meant. Because I don't remember any Dragan Mitrovic from that time. I cannot tell you the precise date which I invoked when I spoke about the entire command of a brigade that was wiped out. The commander informed that the agreed coordinated action did not work very well. It's true that the planned re-subordination should have begun by then, if you are talking about the 20th April. But you see that the brigade commanders warn in the month of May that people are getting killed despite their coordinated action and the re-subordination. One brigade commander said that 100 metres away there was a MUP unit with which they had a previous agreement who would be where and they were not alert enough and careful enough and the entire command of that brigade was wiped out. That was a singular case in that war. It's true that if the date was the 20th of April, it hadn't been finalised yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lazarevic, I'm finding difficulty following some of your evidence just now, because the answer to the question that you were asked at the moment is contained in the final sentence of what you've just said. And really we have to allow Mr. Ivetic to ask the questions the way he wants to ask them, and you have the same obligation as other witnesses have had here, to answer the particular question. And that question only sought to determine whether -- or to clarify whether your order was after the 20th of April, as you confirmed at the end. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, General, you indicated in your direct examination after -- that after the 16th of April, 1999, the orders no longer needed to have the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija title on them and in fact were designated as being Pristina Corps documents, as the prior ones you said were, in fact, apart from that title. That's -- well, here I have to -- here I have to go into the Serbian. We're talking about "zapovesti," not "naredjenje." That's a point where the English word "order" has two Serbian counterparts. And so I apologise, I have to use the Serbian "zapovest" in the transcript. If I can ask you, do you recall that sometime around that same time- I think it was approximately the 20th or the 22nd of April, 1999 - do you recall that General Pavkovic of the 3rd Army and General and Assistant Minister Obrad Stevanovic of the MUP had a debate and a discussion trying to iron out the differing interpretations and meanings of "re-subordination" particularly with respect to Article 17 of the Law of Defence?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My knowledge about that activity, as far as I'm able to recall at this moment, relates to a meeting before the 20th of April, because what I remember is that I was involved, that the army commander had invited me -- or rather, called me up during one night to move towards Pristina. I don't know which installation it was. I cannot locate it precisely. It was late at night. Anyway, we were supposed to meet with someone from the MUP to see how we were going to realise an order that had come from the command of the Supreme Staff on the 18th. So my recollection is that it was that it was on -- before the 20th of April, not on the 20th or the 22nd. It was a meeting late at night in this building in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall that General Stevanovic of the MUP debated the interpretations of Article 17 of the Law on Defence with General Pavkovic, that they were the main participants in this debate or discussion about the implementation of the re-subordination order of the chief of the -- staff of the High Command?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was a debate on this topic. I cannot confirm now whether it was the Article 17 or whatever, but I know the outcome of that brief meeting in the middle of the night. General Stevanovic said that he did not have an order from his Minister of the Interior. He was one of the assistants to the minister, as far as I can remember, and that he could not carry out an order from the chief of the Supreme Command Staff. And the meeting ended at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, were you present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to the discussions, am I correct that there was also a discussion as to martial law or military law and the fact that this was not reaching out to the point where the military would take over all civilian activities and functions in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. I didn't understand whether you were asking me or whether you're quoting something from that meeting. I just don't understand what you're driving at.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... whether the topic -- whether the topics for discussion and debate was discussion over "vojna uprava," military rule in taking over civilian functions from civilian authorities, such as the MUP? Than -- and -- and improper or incorrect interpretations of what the -- what the circumstances and the declaration of war meant.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps this is a matter of interpretation, but this is the first time that I hear anyone in my presence use the term "military rule" during the war or that this was discussed in my presence. And an order of this kind with such provisions created headache to MUP and to -- to me as the Pristina Corps commander. This is quite clear. I spoke about that the other day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, subsequent to these discussions, whether they were on the 18th, 19th, or the 22nd, you issued P2809, which I would ask to be put up on the screen, strictly confidential number 455-183 dated the 28th of April. If we can look at -- we'll wait for the document to come up. Am I correct that this -- whoops. Is this P2809? I'm getting something ... 2809. P2809. This one is apparently 2089. Okay. Now, if we could focus on paragraph 1 in both the B/C/S and the English translation, which is on the screen for this one, where it says: "Engage forces of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia (PJP) manoeuvre detachments and MUP territorial units to carry out combat tasks in the PrK zone. Other forces and institutions continue to remain under the jurisdiction of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia." Would you agree with me that this is a narrower view of re-subordination than had been proposed by the initial order that came down from the Supreme Command Staff and that this narrower interpretation was a result of the discussions that the VJ had with the-- with the MUP personnel? That is, the --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With all due respect for what the Defence counsel has just said, I would like to say that what is written in this document is the result of a document that I drafted in my capacity as the Pristina Corps commander on the 20th of April where I tried to give an interpretation of how this mission impossible, as I called it the other day, could be implemented. Because what is written here is not based on the original document from the 3rd Army command or the Supreme Command Staff. And after that meeting, I never even saw anyone from the MUP. I didn't consult anyone. I did consult with the army commander. And this is an attempt to deal with this thing that is not fully defined under the law and in the order, to make it possible for us at the corps command to carry out this task as much as it was possible. So I couldn't confirm whether this followed after any discussions with the MUP members. And you can see here that I'm referring to the order of the command of the army where he tried to adjust his order to what was actually possible given the situation. And that is the gist of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to follow up on that, this is the first time that Article 17 of the Law on Defence had been actually implemented in practice by the Army of Yugoslavia; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I am expert enough to provide an interpretation of Article 17, but if the Trial Chamber allows me as a layperson with no legal knowledge -- if I were to say anything about Article 17, I would say that this is not -- it is not correct, because it says that the army would be in command of the combat. It is impossible to command the combat. One can only command forces, troops. So I cannot confirm whether this means an attempt to implement Article 17, but it's an attempt on the part of the 3rd Army to implement a task that was given to it by the Supreme Command Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just one or two or questions and then I think we -- Are we at the break point now, Your Honour? Or I think we have five more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I think now is the appropriate time to break, if that's convenient for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Then we'll resume at ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, we still have on the screen, I believe, the exhibit that we had, P2809, your order. I would ask for the second and final page of this exhibit to be placed up on e-court so that I can ask you a few questions relative to the same. Specifically, if I can direct your attention to paragraph 8 of this document. And there it indicates that "PJP detachments will be occasionally engaged in anti-terrorist operations outside their zones in line with the plan of the Pristina Corps Command and the brigade commanders will be duly informed". Do you recall who created this plan of the Pristina Corps command for the PJP redeployment? Or did such a plan exist?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here the subordinate commanders are given a suggestion that if the MUP forces are engaged, those PJP detachments, that a plan would be made, an order. A plan is a set of documents. So we're not talking about a plan that was done at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we look at the enclosed. You are enclosed, and along with this order you had a map showing locations of MUP detachments and a plan of engagement of the joint units with their activities and tasks. Would that be an Odluka map or not? Would it be similar to an Odluka map where both VJ and MUP forces and their deployments are -- are indicated?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not similar. This is an overview map, as far as I can remember. The scale is 1 to 200.000. It includes the whole of Kosovo and Metohija. It is based on the information that the Pristina Corps command knew, about the location of the police units at that time. And the corps command did not get -- and let me tell you now that the regulations stipulated this is an obligation -- the information as to what units, in what area are subordinated to the Pristina Corps and to the brigades, in order to be able to implement the re-subordination order fully. I know that the army commander did not have that, but now I'm talking about the corps command. A map was made where in item 10 I demand that the commanders give me feedback once they ascertained where the MUP units were in order to have at least their current areas of deployment. And let me remind you that the MUP units were rotated in accordance with their plan. And it was impossible to follow that on this map. In item 2, if that's what you wanted me to talk about, the engagement plan in the combat control of the territory, this is a plan in the form of a text of the joint forces. We mean the joint tactical units in the brigade. Every brigade is assigned its zone where it is supposed to control certain roads. And let me conclude that this is an attempt, a blind attempt, so to speak, without any of the substantial elements that have to be given in the order about the units of the MUP that should be under somebody's command. So without this knowledge, the corps command tried to do something, to make certain things possible in a combat situation. So this is the gist of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now, I recall from our early -- from earlier testimony in this case that the initials at the end of military documents are supposed to show the author and the typist or operative who -- who drafted -- who published the -- the particular document. In this case, we have "NP/BV." Which of these initials indicates the author of the document? Because I don't see your initials anywhere on here. Is this a error or can you identify for us who either NP or BV is.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The initials on the left-hand side designate the author of this text, the person who drafted the document. And the ones on the right-hand side indicate the person who actually typed this document out on a typewriter or a computer. It is not a mistake, and the corps commander very rarely drafts these documents. I did do so on several occasions, as you were able to see. Particularly, when this dealt with the compliance with the international humanitarian law or topics of that nature where I demand full compliance with some things. I really cannot recognise those initials. I don't know who in the corps command with these initials drafted this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are they not the initials of General Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Your Honour, Mr. President, absolutely not. It is impossible for him to draft a document for me -- for my signature. Yes, he does have the same initials, but it is absolutely out of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What rank of officer, then, would normally draft such a document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the operations organ of the corps command, there were people with the ranks of major and colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you can't help us even after thinking carefully about it to identify who NP was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point in time, I cannot. If during the course of the day I manage to focus and remember, I will very gladly try to tell you who these initials belong to. I know it's not Radojko Stefanovic, the man operations man who is often the author of these documents. It's not Ratko Tesovic, who was his assistant either. Now, I can just guess, but I cannot remember anything else at this point. I will try to focus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Whose initials are BV?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a lady typist, Biljana Veljovic or Veljkovic, who worked at the corps command as a civilian employed in the army. A professional employed at the corps command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I think that's all I need for this document. I'd like to now return to some of the -- some of the "zapovests" or -- or orders that we have seen after this date to see how they treated the matters. I think -- well, I guess for the sake of efficiency, why don't we deal with 6D704, which was the one that we had discussed at the beginning of my cross-examination with respect to the item about the building of the joint -- building of the Pristina command in its peacetime location as being a -- the command centre for this action of Bajgora dva or Bajgora 2. This is a "zapovest" for Bajgora 2, as I've indicated.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the top it says it's from the command of the Pristina Corps , strictly confidential number 455-182. And it's dated, as you indicated, the 4th of May, 1999. If we can look at 5.1 and 5.2, which should be on the second page at the bottom of the -- of the document, the second -- the second page, bottom of the page, leading onto the third page, the assignments for the units that are to be involved. And I think we can actually skip ahead to the third page in the B/C/S. I'll short circuit the analysis of this since we don't have an English that we can really follow. And here we have on this page assignments given for VTOs at 5.3 and 5.4 to engage in coordinated action with the MUP forces. And then at 5.5, we have the -- we have an order -- or, excuse me pardon me. We have an assignment or task for the 35th Detachment of the PJP of the MUP. Would you agree with me that as far as section 5.5 is concerned, that there are no army units listed in this tasking paragraph and that the MUP unit is the only one that is to undertake the action together with the other forces enumerated?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right. As for such documents, orders, after the date envisaged for re-subordination, there are a few of them. However, I claim with full responsibility that although it comes from the war and directly issued to the MUP, re-subordination not carried out in accordance with combat rules and there are reports of units to confirm that after all brigade commanders will come and testify about that, so I don't want to take up the Court's time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And indeed re-subordination would have been played out at the brigade level anyway. The Pristina Corps command did not -- strike that. Would you agree with me and the appraisal of General Radinovic, I believe it was, that the coordination would have been carried out at the brigade level?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I have to say for the sake of clarity and precision, coordination is one activity and command and re-subordination another activity. I agree with you that at brigade level, which is what otherwise happened, coordination and coordinated activity -- however, re-subordination did not happen. That means a chain of command within which this unit of the police would be. You are asking me whether I agree with a comment made by General Radinovic regarding re-subordination. In some parts I disagree with him. He's not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But as -- but as far as the "zapovest" order itself is concerned, this both -- this one and the other ones that exist for 1999 plan for specific and detailed tasks of the MUP in their text; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With all due respect, the head of state issued an order and it was not carried out. I am not denying what is written here, but I am saying what the actual state of affairs was. The factual situation did not correspond to this, as had been ordered, and I could not change the decision of the army commander. He did not say, "There are no more orders from the army commander on the re-subordination of the MUP." Finally, at some point we are going to get to these documents. And as we say in Serbian, even -- you can even give up on that. But that time had not come at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, General, you say you want to talk about the factual circumstances as they were on the terrain. With respect to this particular engagement or action Bajgora -- I think -- Bajgora 2, was the coordinated and cooperative joint action of the VJ and the MUP actually carried out in the field in a manner where the tasks undertaken were consistent with those tasks that were laid out in the "zapovest" order?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cooperation and coordination did happen, but the chain of command was an independent one, as far as the police unit is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As -- as far as the implementation of this "zapovest," did the action take place in -- involving the engagement of both MUP and VJ forces?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean this action specifically, without analysing the content of the combat reports, I cannot confirm anything, because indeed there was some planning of some actions that had not been carried through. I know that there were some actions that had indeed been carried through and that all these relations remained at the level of coordination, cooperation, and coordinated activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to those actions that you say were realised on the level of coordination and cooperation, were the -- were the tasks of those operations successfully achieved? When you say "realised," I presume you mean implemented. Were the goals of the operation successfully achieved? For those that you say you do have knowledge of that were realised?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few actions -- I would say a couple of these actions, not operations, were carried out properly from the point of view of cooperation and coordination. Some, such as Jablanica, in the final stage of the war, were not due to different problems, losses, and some other problems. People couldn't really find their way. So my answer is some to a larger degree, some to a lesser degree, but here I am not testifying to any problems there in respect of cooperation. Yes, people worked to the best of their knowledge and ability. I'm just pointing out that the system of command remained separate throughout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, did the 35th Detachment of the PJP carry out the task which is referred to in paragraph 5.5?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, I have just answered to counsel that at this point in time I really do not know whether this task had fully been carried out. I am just asking you to accept this information that I am providing; namely, that according to our plan, the brigade commander from this area is going to come and testify as a witness here, and with your permission, my Defence will take upon itself this obligation that we clarify this at that point in time. I really do not know now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It would be much more helpful to the Trial Chamber to have clarification now, when the issue has arisen for the first time. You will -- I'm sure you'll understand why that's the case. And you've been able to give us a great deal of detail about how particular operations were actually executed. But you're saying you just can't help us on this one at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot, Your Honour, Mr. President, at this point in time, because this document is one that I haven't seen now. As for the information I've had so far, they can best be seen from the combat reports of the units, reporting as to whether things had been done in a certain way or not. Now, I can try within the briefest period of time possible to see whether we have some documents available in order to assist the Trial Chamber, but just off the cuff I cannot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if a particular -- if a particular unit of the MUP engaging in what you call "a coordinated" or "cooperative action with VJ forces," if that MUP unit had not undertaken the tasks as outlined in a "zapovest," would you expect that to be in -- contained in the post-combat report of that particular action?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember some reports, as I've said, not specifically in relation to this situation, when commanders quite simply reported that the MUP unit had not come or that the representative of the police had said that they did not have sufficient forces for carrying out that task. Recently I had such documents in my hands. As for this specific action, though, I cannot say either "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we can focus a little bit more on -- let's see. Let's go to 6D712. This is a document that was previously used with another witness, so it's already marked for identification, for the last month, it would appear. This is the "zapovest," order for Drenica-1. Since we've already gone through it with the other witness, I would just highlight a few things. If we can focus on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have you not done something about getting this translated?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the priority with CLSS is for documents that are not into evidence that will be in -- used in evidence with upcoming witnesses. The MFI documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Surely -- surely top priority is documents which have already been used but have not been translated. Common sense would tell us that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, common sense would say that prioritization is prioritization not removal of documents and a lot of times with CLSS --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, now Mr. Ivetic; just deal with the point that arises here. Surely first priority must be documents already submitted marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will submit not, Your Honours. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I'm telling you here and now it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will change that then with CLSS. That will require another submission on my behalf with them and more meetings with them, which I will gladly undertake, Your Honours. But that was not what was discussed at the meetings previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think it's something that goes without saying, frankly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now -- I thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could move to page -- let me just find my place. One moment, please. For purposes of allowing us to make sense of the next exhibit I would use, I would like to turn to page 4 of this document, item 5.6 -- 5.6, dealing with the tasking of the 124th Intervention Brigade of the MUP and the 122nd Intervention Brigade of the MUP for this action. And then I would like to ask you to turn to the final page, page 7 in e-court, and I would ask you to read section 14 for us, General, and then in -- and that's the last page. And with respect to item 14, after you read it for us, could you explain for us the acronym "chief of the OOPiO," who that is, whether that is a police or army post. If you would, please, sir, after reading for us section 14 in its entirety, the four lines, beginning with [B/C/S spoken]?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Coordination among elements of the combat disposition during the planning, organisation, preparation, and execution of combat activities in the area of Drenica shall be carried out by the team of the command of the Pristina Corps headed by the chief of the organ for operations affairs and training, that is, the mainstay of planning, organisation, and execution of combat activities." That is an officer from the command of the Pristina Corps, the head of the operations and training affairs organ. It has nothing to do with the police. As you can see, I cannot issue orders to anyone from the police either.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with respect to this chief of the OOPiO, am I correct that this is in fact the Colonel Radojko Stefanovic that you mentioned several moment ago and with respect to another question, as the person who planned this action?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Colonel Radojko Stefanovic. As for those initials, RT, Ratko Tesovic, is his assistant, who authored this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would Colonel Stefanovic be the one who created the Odluka map, the decision map for this particular action?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is one of the mainstays of planning the use of units in the corps command. He is at the head of this organ that prepares these combat documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was this action undertaken and realised on the ground?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, towards the end of May, yes, this action was taken and carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did the 124th Intervention Brigade of the MUP participate in the action in the manner foreseen by the tasking set forth in the zapovest zadaci udince [phoen], assignments for units?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for all documents, all situations throughout the war, regardless of what was written somewhere, I assert that it was only at the level of coordination and cooperation with fully-separated chains of command, as we call this in this courtroom; that is to say, command of units of the army and units of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But in regards to that coordinated and cooperation act - "sadvesta" - I don't know if its been translated that way in the Serbian. But with respect to the "sadejstvo," on the part of the MUP and the VJ for purposes of this action did the 125th Intervention Brigade of the MUP in this coordinated action -- not comply but operate and undertake tasks that are the tasks that were laid out in the "zapovest" decision, the "zapovest" order?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this moment I do not have any other knowledge, any specific knowledge, to be able to say no. They often took part in carrying out a task in coordination with the MUP, but really and before my eyes I do not have a document that I had recently seen so that I could say precisely and categorically that this was the case. There is no reason for me to say that there was no coordinated action or cooperation, but I cannot be more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you know -- strike that. I saw a map flash up onto the screen. Do we have another page to this exhibit or not? If we can go to the next page of the -- the exhibit, then. I could see -- hopefully ... It's a little bit difficult to read. In any event, let me -- well, let me -- let me call up -- Is that -- can you see, sir, is that Radojko Stefanovic on the bottom right -- the bottom right of the document? If we can zoom in on the bottom right of the document. Is that the chief of the OOPiO Pukovnik Colonel Radojko Stefanovic of the Pristina Corps, who is the --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can zoom up to the upper left portion of this, we see there that you, General, have -- are the -- are the officer tasked with authorising the -- the Odluka itself that this -- the decision itself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I apologise, this one's not that clear. If -- for sake of short circuiting this if we can have 6D1413 up on the screen. I believe it's a cleaner copy of the same -- of the same document. 6D1413?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: For the sake of the transcript, it's 6D1413. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And if we could zoom in on the top third of the document. There we go. This would be fine. Perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you see there the 37th Brigade in big letters and then next to it in smaller script the "124th Intervention Brigade of the MUP and the 122nd Intervention Brigade of the MUP being depicted upon this Odluka, map, of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- and am I correct that the movements of this formation are depicted on the map? We could probably scroll down a little bit to get the full -- there. That should be fine for this purpose. Are the movements of this particular formation also recorded on this Odluka map? I know it would be a lot easier if we had the colour maps. I have a request outstanding but have only received partial compliance.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not in dispute, because "zapovest," the command regulates the way of engagement of this police unit. Whether this schematic precisely reflects it, I don't know, because I can't see whether it's the 37th Motorised or whether it's part of one or another police brigade. But this is in keeping with the prior "zapovest" command that accompanies this. The map accompanies and reflects the -- the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you say "this is in keeping with the prior zapovest," are you saying that the assignments specified herein are in keeping with the prior "zapovest" for both VJ and MUP units?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a map of the decision, an attachment to the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we see here what we -- what was difficult to see on the prior copy. We see here a bunch of circles with numbers in them throughout the map. And if we zoom out, we'll see that they indeed cover the entire region. Am I correct that in fact this Odluka map is one of those coded or encoded maps that one of the prior witnesses made reference to which allows for communications between units to both give and receive locations that the enemy forces cannot have access to, by referring to -- to numbers on -- on this map?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map is not exactly consistent with that testimony you are referring to. It's a so-called encoded map. It's an auxiliary document. Whereas, this one is a compilation both of the decision map and the encoded map with code names for certain points, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- and such a map would be given to all units and forces taking part in a -- in an action for -- that is to say, the -- the portion of the map dealing with a particular unit would be given to it prior to undertaking the realisation of a particular action, a joint coordinated cooperative action,"sadejstvo"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map was not in this form submitted to anyone. It's done in two copies. One is in the corps command and the second is possibly for the army command. Whereas, for subordinated units, only excerpts of the map are made. The section of the map that is relevant to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And these excerpts or sections of the map would be given to all units taking part, whether they're VJ or MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In circumstances and in situations when it was ordered to a re-subordinated force that if re-subordination had not been effected, that there is instead coordinated action, then the police unit cannot and should not receive a map like this. The planning authority in that police unit makes its own map, and that map is to be approved by his own superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What is the bases of your statement that the planning authority in that police unit makes its own map and the map is to be approved by its own superior? Have you ever seen in 1999 any map prepared by the MUP of the Republic of Serbia for undertaking a joint action, as you call it, "sadejstvo," coordinated cooperative action with the VJ?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the principle of the combat use of the army that cannot be effected without an order from the superior command. Following that principle, it is my opinion as an officer that no unit can be used unless its own superior ordered it. Whether this order will be in the form of the map or whether the superior will say, "Go ahead and do what you want," I really cannot speculate. This is the principle of command that applies in the army. It is done through a decision map. My map or a map of some other commander cannot be a basis for using a police unit unless there has been re-subordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we conclude from that answer, sir, that you in fact have not seen a card -- or pardon me. Excuse me -- a map for an action prepared by any police organ for the engagement of MUP forces in a joint action with the VJ?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen the map. I haven't seen the "zapovest" command. I haven't seen the other documents. But it does not mean that they were not made. I do not doubt that the MUP has its own principles, regulations, and I'm only talking from the viewpoint of which military document can apply to what.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's see. I'm trying to economize my time. I think I will revert back to 1998 for a second to try and make use of the remaining minutes that we have and make some headway here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You were asked about the action undertaken in April -- pardon me. Pardon me. I'm -- we're still dealing with 1999. But dealing with the action at Rugovska Klisura that was in April of 1999, Mr. Ackerman asked you about that and he asked you about the document authored by General Pavkovic to General Ojdanic saying that he could -- that Pavkovic could not implement suggestions because this was an action planned by the police. I take it you have no knowledge of any Odluka map for that action, or do you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard from other witnesses in this courtroom that there was some sort of map related to the Rugova gorge, Rugovska Klisura, that it was even in the office of the head of state, but I really cannot visualise that map now. I cannot recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: From my recollection, the witnesses - at least, I believe General Vasiljevic - mentioned that he and General Ojdanic saw General Pavkovic going -- no? Well, strike that then. The testimony I recall is that General Pavkovic brought a map to President Milosevic for this action. Is that your recollection as well, General Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we heard in this courtroom, I believe, from General Curcin, that was the same topic. He said the army commander had been to see President Milosevic with some sort of map and that map then hanged in the office of the chief of the Supreme Command Staff. But I really cannot remember it. If you find it and if you show it to me, maybe I will be able to be of assistance, but I cannot tell you now which specific map it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll try to make it easy for you. You've talked several times about how things are done in the army according to the military principles and doctrines of commanding, et cetera. Based upon the fact that when viewing this map we heard testimony that General Ojdanic sent suggestions to General Pavkovic and, indeed, we have General Pavkovic acknowledging receipt of that in his documentation, can we conclude that the map that these two army officers were looking at was a map drafted by -- drafted and/or approved by an army officer, since they did not direct any suggestions to any organ within the MUP?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can recall anything at this moment, it's this document called "Suggestions." In one passage, it says that the chief of the Supreme Command Staff requires the army commander to modify his decision. Is this an answer to your question? It is up to you. But I really am not able to offer any further comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, I think that suffices for -- for purposes of that. Do you have knowledge, as commander of the Pristina Corps in April of 1999, whether in fact VJ units participated in the operation for Rugovska Klisura that started in April, and I believe you indicated, went all the way through May?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it -- a part of the 125th Motorised Brigade did take part in that action that lasted a bit longer. That's the Rugovska Klisura action.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the document Mr. Ackerman presented said that the operation had been planned by the police. Did the police also plan the engagement and use of the 125th Motorised Brigade of the Pristina Corps? Is it possible for a police unit to plan and direct the engagement of a VJ unit?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's impossible. It's absolutely impossible. But with the leave of the Honourable Trial Chamber, if I can be of assistance, I can say that to the best of my recollection, even before that order of the chief of Supreme Command Staff concerning coordinated action, the police planned to perform its own action in that area. Later on there was coordination with the 2nd Army between the army and the police, and that took a while. I want to draw your attention to the fact that the police planned its own action, the army planned its own actions, and in areas where they found themselves close by, that -- they worked together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this a convenient point to interrupt you, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We shall adjourn now and resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 14th day of November, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
